origin: ts.mbt — found by probing `Object.defineProperty`, which no harness had ever generated
what: The dead-property pass deleted descriptor flags as unread keys: `{ value: 1, enumerable: true }` became `{ value: 1 }`. Every `Object.defineProperty` default is `false`, so dropping a `true` flag inverts it — `Object.keys` stopped seeing the property, `writable: true` made a later assignment throw in the module's strict mode, and `configurable: true` made `delete` throw. It was NOT the mangler renaming them: `get`, `set` and `value` happened to be in `mangler_builtin_reserved_properties` already — incidentally, under Map/Set and the iterator protocol — so `value` surviving made the shape look safe while the three flags nobody else had needed were absent. There is a `// Property descriptor` group now. A `false` flag is harmless to drop since it matches the default, which is what made two of the three original probes pass and is covered here as `defaultedHolder`.
